article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 80% Sativa / 20% Indica
Genetics: Blueberry Muffin × Tangie
Breeder: Humboldt Seed Company
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: Not specified
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet and tart grapefruit, plum, and citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 50 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: September 20 – October 5
Indoor Yield: 450 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 600 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Squirt has a sharper personality than the sugary fruit flavors that dominate many modern cannabis menus. Its combination of sweetness, tartness, and aromatic peel gives this weed strain a recognizable identity, backed by a pairing of berry-rich Blueberry Muffin and citrus-heavy Tangie. Humboldt Seed Company selected this cultivar for its aromatic expression, then developed it into a fast-flowering, sativa-dominant line. Purple and green flowers add visual interest, but the real attraction lies in the relationship between its vivid citrus character and a generally upbeat experience. For growers, approximately seven weeks of indoor flowering makes it an intriguing alternative to longer-running sativa hybrids.
Genetics and Lineage

Squirt originated from Blueberry Muffin × Tangie, with the standout plant identified as BBM × Tang #118 during Humboldt Seed Company’s 10,000-plant phenotype hunt. A phenotype hunt compares individual plants from breeding populations, allowing breeders to select combinations of aroma, growth, flower structure, and other observable characteristics. Subsequent breeding focused on retaining the distinctive citrus expression. Backcrossing in the line’s development helps explain why the breeder emphasizes aromatic consistency even when individual plants differ in coloration.

Blueberry Muffin supplies a substantial fruit-oriented background. Humboldt identifies its parents as Purple Panty Dropper and Razzleberry, a combination associated with blueberry, sweet baked-goods aromas, and purple expression. The parent’s comparatively short flowering period also provides useful context for the offspring’s quick finish, although no single inherited trait can be assigned to one parent with certainty. Plum and softer fruit impressions sit behind the dominant citrus, providing depth that separates the cultivar from a purely orange-smelling selection.

Tangie contributes the other major branch of the family. DNA Genetics describes its ancestry as California Orange × Skunk #1 , connecting its tangerine character to classic citrus and Skunk breeding. That lineage brings a contrasting aromatic direction to Blueberry Muffin’s dessert-like sweetness. Squirt Auto is a separate breeding product that adds Blueberry Muffin Auto genetics; its seed-to-harvest schedule should not be confused with the photoperiod cultivar’s flowering time.
Effects and Experience

The most characteristic expectation is an initially uplifting, energetic high. After inhalation, an early shift in mood and sensory attention may make music, conversation, or an unhurried creative activity feel more engaging. Some people experience this as a relatively functional form of intoxication, with less immediate heaviness than they associate with sedating weed. However, “functional” describes a subjective impression, not preserved reaction time or unimpaired reasoning. THC can alter memory, coordination, and judgment even when the person feels alert and comfortable.

The experience can soften as it progresses. A lively beginning may give way to more relaxed, dreamy sensations, with physical ease becoming more prominent as the initial stimulation fades. Larger amounts can push that transition toward drowsiness, particularly in someone with limited tolerance. There is no universal sequence: the same flower may feel sociable to one person and distracting to another. Amount consumed, recent cannabis use, fatigue, and the setting all influence whether the uplifting phase remains pleasant or becomes mentally overwhelming.

At approximately 20% THC, a small quantity can still produce substantial effects. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, and anxiety are possible, while repeated inhalations taken too quickly can exceed the intended intensity before the initial response is fully apparent. Edibles made with this cultivar require separate consideration because oral THC has a delayed onset and often a longer duration. A current laboratory label and a measured approach are more useful than assuming a citrus-flavored sativa will always feel light.
Medical Benefits

Medical interest in this hybrid centers on the possibility of symptom relief without immediate, pronounced sedation. Certain cannabis preparations have shown modest benefits for some chronic pain conditions, but those findings do not establish Squirt as a clinically validated treatment. A patient may find that physical discomfort becomes less intrusive while mood improves, yet another may experience little relief or unacceptable impairment. The relevant variables include the actual cannabinoid content, dose, route of administration, and underlying condition. Sativa dominance alone cannot identify which pain symptoms might respond.

An uplifting experience may also appeal to people dealing with stress or emotional strain, although temporary enjoyment should not be confused with treatment for depression or an anxiety disorder. THC can worsen anxiety, especially when the dose is higher than the person tolerates. Likewise, a reputation for energy does not establish effectiveness for ADHD, chronic fatigue, or poor concentration. Someone sensitive to stimulating marijuana may find the cultivar uncomfortable even at a relatively modest amount. Its unspecified CBD content means consumers should not assume the flower delivers a balanced THC-to-CBD preparation.

For medical use, the strongest practical starting point is a tested product with clearly labeled cannabinoid content. Patients taking medicines that cause sedation, or managing conditions affected by cannabis, should discuss use with their clinician. Tracking the amount consumed and the actual change in symptoms offers a more meaningful basis for evaluating benefit than choosing solely by a strain name or broad effects description.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweet-tart grapefruit leads the profile, with the breeder also identifying plum. That combination gives the aroma both brightness and a rounder fruit body: the citrus supplies the sharp edge, while sweeter notes keep it from seeming one-dimensional. Depending on the plant and cure, the balance may lean toward peel-like citrus, juicy fruit, or a softer berry background.

The breeder emphasizes both monoterpenes and sesquiterpenes, two groups of aromatic compounds found in cannabis resin. Monoterpenes are generally more volatile, while sesquiterpenes tend to be less volatile; the mixture helps shape the aroma during handling and consumption. A grapefruit-forward smell does not, by itself, prove that limonene dominates. Nor does Tangie parentage guarantee the same terpene ranking found in a sample of the parent. Batch testing is necessary to identify measured compounds and their proportions, while smelling the flower reveals how those compounds interact with the broader volatile mixture.

Preserving that sharp citrus character requires attention after harvest. Heat and unnecessary air exposure can strip away lighter aromatic notes, leaving the flower less expressive even when its cannabinoid content remains substantial. Gentle drying, a careful cure, and cool, dark storage help maintain the contrast between tart citrus and sweeter fruit. Resin abundance makes the cultivar interesting for extraction, but visible frost does not establish a guaranteed hash yield. Trichome characteristics and processing method determine how effectively a particular plant translates into a concentrate.
Growing Information

The plant’s relatively slender, potentially tall structure deserves consideration before flowering begins. A short bloom period does not necessarily mean a compact canopy, and vegetative growth should be planned around the available headroom. Gentle branch training and appropriately timed topping can distribute growth, while a trellis or individual supports help carry flowering branches. Leave enough space for light to reach multiple sites rather than allowing a few dominant tops to overshadow the rest.

Approximately 50 days of indoor flowering provides a useful schedule, but maturity should be checked on the plant. Flower development and trichome appearance across several representative sites provide better guidance than harvesting every phenotype on the same date. Purple pigmentation may vary considerably, and green flowers are not evidence that a plant is incorrectly identified. Anthocyanin expression depends on genetics and environmental conditions; deliberately chilling the crop to force color can compromise growth. Consistent irrigation, appropriate nutrition, and adequate airflow matter more to finished quality than maximizing purple coloration.

Outdoors, the September 20–October 5 harvest window can be advantageous in regions where later-finishing marijuana encounters worsening autumn weather. The dates still depend on local conditions, latitude, and the individual plant. Choose a location with useful sunlight and moving air, and inspect flowers after rain rather than treating the earlier finish as protection against mold. The breeder’s potential yield figures describe favorable outcomes, not guaranteed harvest weights. Plant size, root space, canopy management, and weather can change production substantially. Once harvested, space the flowers adequately during drying to protect both their resin quality and distinctive citrus aroma.
FAQ

Is Squirt indica or sativa? Humboldt Seed Company classifies the photoperiod cultivar as approximately 80% sativa and 20% indica. What strains make Squirt? Its confirmed parents are Blueberry Muffin and Tangie, with the original selected plant labeled BBM × Tang #118.

What does Squirt weed taste like? Sweet and tart grapefruit is the primary flavor, supported by plum and other fruit impressions. How much THC does it contain? The breeder lists an average around 20%, but finished flower should be evaluated using its own laboratory results rather than assuming every harvest matches that figure.

How long does Squirt take to flower? The photoperiod version flowers indoors in approximately 50 days, with a listed outdoor harvest from September 20 through October 5. That flowering period excludes vegetative growth. Squirt Auto follows a different schedule, typically described as approximately 80–90 days from seed to harvest.
Final Thoughts on Squirt

Squirt’s value lies in a distinctive grapefruit expression paired with a comparatively quick flowering period and an often uplifting opening to the high. Blueberry Muffin and Tangie provide clear genetic context, while variable purple coloration adds interest without defining flower quality. Consumers drawn to sharp citrus and a potentially energetic experience have good reasons to explore a tested batch. Growers should pay particular attention to canopy space, flower maturity, and preserving volatile aromas after harvest. When those details come together, this cultivar offers an individual character that extends beyond its soda-inspired name.
